stops.title: Device, Inverter, Layout, Process
stops.body: Explore device structures, illustrative CMOS inverter circuits, schematic layouts and, in Process, how a device is made. The selected architecture carries across modes. Layout simplifies the layer stack and vertical geometry.

stops.title: Compare architectures
stops.body: Explore four device architectures on one possible scaling roadmap: FinFET, nanosheet FET, inner-wall forksheet and CFET. Tap an architecture button, or Compare to see the examples side by side.

stops.title: Orbit, pan, zoom, inspect
stops.body: Drag with one finger to orbit. Two fingers to pan. Pinch to zoom. Tap any layer to see what it's made of.

stops.title: Views
stops.body: Choose a preset 3D overview or a view along or across the channel. Presets vary by scene; architecture-specific details appear in the specialized views.

stops.title: Section
stops.body: Slide to cut the model open on any axis, or pull the layers apart. Display holds the sheet's see-through, slow rotate and the other display switches.

stops.title: Layers
stops.body: Hide any single layer to see what's underneath it — or hide a whole group, or everything, with one tap.

stops.title: Specs
stops.body: Read model dimensions and design notes. On individual Device scenes, tap a capacitance row to highlight the modeled coupling. Values are geometry-only estimates, not measurements or a field-solver extraction.

stops.title: Steps (Process mode)
stops.body: In Process, the Steps tab takes the place of Specs: every fabrication step with what it shows, the source it follows and what the model leaves out. Step with the arrows on the stage or press play. Show every operation adds the resist, exposure, etch and fill substeps; between nanosheet steps 3 and 4.1, choose how the stack lines are printed: direct print, SADP or SAQP. The SADP and SAQP chips show those routes on their own. So far the nanosheet has a flow; the other architectures are coming.

stops.title: Story
stops.body: Read the concepts, trade-offs and limitations behind the architecture. Open About for Credits and linked Technical references.
